source.note: Installed build differs from the retained 1.3.6.1921 target; this finding is scoped to 1.3.9.2055.

method: Static arm64 disassembly of the original executable with lldb/otool. ObjC selector stubs resolved through __objc_selrefs; no code executed and no installed file modified.
findings: previousTrackCommand handler dispatches command 7, or 13 when useSeekForSkipKeys is true (nextTrackCommand: 6 or 12).
initWithPlayerDelegate: stores halfword 1 at ivar offset 8, leaving useSeekForSkipKeys (offset 9) false; no caller of setUseSeekForSkipKeys: was found in the executable.
Command 7 (0x10049bd0c) constructs the native skip-prev command (CommandOptions base, bool at +0x38), sets the bool to 1 and calls the player vtable slot +0x50.
The JSON command decoder at 0x101d22308 constructs the same struct and reads key "allow_seeking" (0x10250969f) into +0x38.
Command 13 (seek mode) reads the current player state and seeks relative to position; it is not used when useSeekForSkipKeys is false.
conclusion: macOS media-key/Now Playing Previous sends SkipPrev with allow_seeking=true, the same command as the playback-bar Previous button. The player, not the media bridge, chooses between restarting the current item and the previous track.
limits: previousTrackCommand.isEnabled follows PlayerState byte +0x2e (same byte as seekBackwardCommand); the upstream field feeding that byte was not mapped. The Dart bridge uses the playback-bar admission (canSkipPrevious || canSeek).
No live original capture of the outgoing command was made.
